transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mayer (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood Product), Marta Ruiz (Apex ML), Devon Park (Apex Infra), Sunil Iyer (Apex SRE)

Summary: Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8), quality/latency tradeoffs, and pilot scoping. Priya demoed Redwood Optimize UI and shared example plots.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro  im Jordan AE, this is Priya our SE and Liam on product. you all good with agenda?
[00:18] Marta: yep, thanks. want to see INT8 vs FP8 impacts, our main metric is F1 on entity extraction and 75ms p95 target if possible, but cost is also big factor.
[00:35] Priya: great, that's helpful. we'll run through the quant profiles, show you the benchmark sheets, then talk pilot and security. i pulled up the Optimize dashboard  if you look at the quantization tab...
[01:05] Priya: so first, INT8 tends to give the biggest latency wins, about 30-50% token throughput improvement vs fp16 on our tests, but quality can drop depending on model and task, we usually see 1-4% F1 drop for NER, sometimes more on heavy reasoning prompts. fp8 is kind of a middle ground, less regression than int8 but also less latency gain.
[01:45] Devon: when you say 30-50% faster, is that on GPU A100 or on T4? we run mixed infra, mostly a100 and some t4-ish nodes.
[02:05] Priya: these numbers are mostly on A100 and H100 families. on older T4/RTX stuff the gains are smaller, and some toolchains don't support fp8 widely yet, so implementation matters.
[02:30] Liam: quick note, our runtime picks kernels per device, so fp8 kernels are chosen where available and we fall back to fp16-safe paths otherwise, that fallback can change latency slightly.
[02:50] Marta: ok and on quality  can we see examples?
[03:05] Priya: yeah i'll pull up the quality-vs-latency plot  here's a screenshot, shared link in chat: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/apex-int8-fp8.csv (link for internal) the top chart shows F1 delta vs baseline fp16 and bottom shows p95 latency.
[03:40] Priya: for one of our NER workloads, fp8 averaged about 0.8% F1 loss and 20% latency improvement; int8 was ~2.6% F1 loss and 42% latency improvement, so tradeoffs are pretty task dependent.
[04:10] Sunil: the ~2.6% F1 loss on int8, is that consistent across prompt lengths? we have a lot of short chats and some long docs.
[04:30] Priya: good question  quality regressions can correlate with sequence length and activation distributions, short prompts sometimes fare better, long-context summarization can amplify delta. we usually recommend running a small eval set of representative prompts.
[04:55] Jordan: to be explicit operationally, you can start hosted with fp8 to get quicker wins without a dedicated procurement, then if you want predictable throughput we can do Dedicated pilot with pinned quant profile.
[05:20] Marta: on Dedicated, do you support VPC/private deployments? our security team needs VPC + KMS and SOC2 evidence.
[05:35] Liam: yes, Private/Dedicated supports customer VPCs, KMS integration, and we can share SOC2 artifacts. we'll coordinate with your security reviewer.
[05:55] Devon: any difference in how quantization is done on Private vs Hosted? like can we supply custom quant profiles?
[06:10] Priya: you can supply a profile and we can ingest it  Optimize supports uploading per-model quantization profiles and testing them. for Dedicated we can run onboarding with your profile and verify quality/latency.
[06:30] Jordan: i'd flag that custom profiles sometimes need a brief kernel tune  we can include that in the pilot scope.
[06:45] Marta: can you walk through the benchmark sheet columns quickly?
[06:55] Priya: sure  columns: prompt_id, seq_len, baseline_fp16_p95, fp8_p95, int8_p95, baseline_f1, fp8_f1, int8_f1, token_count, model_version. we also include raw latency CSVs for each run. note the CSVs may have some transcription of model names wrong  sometimes shows redwood-m-v1b instead of full name because of export quirks.
[07:35] Devon: do you do statistical significance checks? we're small sample wary.
[07:45] Priya: we run bootstrap intervals and include p-values in the spreadsheet for key metrics, but for production decisions we recommend running the pilot with your real traffic to validate.
[08:05] Marta: if we do pilot, what's the minimal size? we were thinking 1k prompts and 10 qps for a week.
[08:20] Jordan: that's reasonable as a smoke test. for throughput numbers we'll need a bit more, but 1k prompts to test quality + a couple hours of sustained qps for latency shape is fine.
[08:40] Sunil: for the pilot will logs/audit be available? we need request-level tracing and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[08:55] Liam: yes, Dedicated/Private includes trace hooks and audit logs; we can forward to your S3 or your logging endpoint, and we support syslog/forwarders. KMS for key wrap as well.
[09:20] Marta: any gotchas about FP8  i heard some models have instabilities?
[09:30] Priya: FP8 tooling is maturing. some older ops or custom kernels may not be fp8-safe and could produce numerical drift; we flag those models in the catalog and often suggest mixed-precision fallback. also tokenizer edge cases can amplify errors.
[09:55] Devon: oh can you do automatic rollback if quality drifts after deployment?
[10:05] Liam: yes, our rollout controls include automatic fallback to baseline model or different quant profile if error rates or quality metrics cross thresholds. it's part of the deployment policy.
[10:25] Jordan: i'll show the demo: opening Optimize, quant profiles page...
[10:40] Priya: here you can simulate latency vs quality by sliding the profile; watch the predicted p95 and expected F1 delta. this is based on historical runs and is an estimate but usually close.
[11:10] Priya: demo note: the simulator uses cached KV stats, so it can be optimistic; we include a confidence band in the UI.
[11:30] Marta: can you export the simulation results as csv?
[11:40] Priya: yes export button in top-right  i'll export and attach the file.
[12:00] [file posted in chat: apex-optimize-sim-20260322.csv]
[12:15] Marta: nice, we'll review that.
[12:25] Devon: cost question  how do you price quantized models? is it per-token same as fp16 or discounted?
[12:40] Jordan: pricing is per-token but we offer unit-cost recommendations depending on quant profile and batching  for Dedicated pilots we can propose effective per-token pricing that reflects lower infra cost from quantized runs. i'll include a sample pricing in the quote.
[13:05] Priya: another operational point: batching behavior changes with lower precision because throughput is higher, so p95 can vary with batching thresholds; Optimize suggests batching configs per-profile.
[13:30] Sunil: can you show typical latency numbers for a 512 token prompt on H100 with int8 vs fp8 vs fp16?
[13:45] Priya: quick numbers from recent runs  fp16 p95 ~ 210ms, fp8 p95 ~165ms, int8 p95 ~120ms on same hardware and model family. these are approximate and vary with sequence distribution.
[14:20] Marta: those are significant. how about cost per 1M tokens?
[14:30] Jordan: ballpark  on Dedicated our internal units show a 30-45% reduction in infra cost with int8 compared to fp16 after amortizing GPU utilization, fp8 is around 15-25%. exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[15:00] Priya: i'll highlight one example row  prompt 342 had weird drop in int8 quality, looked fine in fp8, that row shows token overflow due to micro-batching. it's why we like to run a small A/B with your prompts.
[15:30] Devon: what's the pilot timeline if we greenlight next week? we have procurement windows for April.
[15:45] Jordan: quick timeline: share prompts and QPS by Mar 27, we set up Dedicated pilot in 3-5 business days provisioning, run 1-2 week validation, then decision. procurement can start in parallel, we'll send contract template.
[16:05] Marta: security specifics  can you provide SOC2, ISO27001 docs and a short note on data retention and deletion?
[16:20] Liam: yes SOC2 and ISO artifacts available, we have data retention controls and customer-managed retention windows in Private. we'll attach the security pack.
[16:40] Sunil: any need to whitelist IPs for VPC peering?
[16:50] Liam: yes a small set of egress/ingress rules; we'll send the network runbook with CIDR ranges.
[17:05] Priya: back to model quality, one more tip: sometimes mixed profiling (fp8 for encoder layers, float for decoder) can give good tradeoffs; Optimize supports layered profiles per model.
[17:30] Marta: is that automated or manual?
[17:35] Priya: currently manual upload of layered profile but we're working on automated suggestions based on your eval.
[17:50] Devon: any competitors we should consider for this pilot?
[17:55] Jordan: folks often compare to Scale AI inference and managed vendors; And some use Anthropic/custom stacks. tradeoffs are support for private deployments and the runtime kernel maturity.
[18:20] Marta: ok, action items recap?
[18:25] Jordan: recap: Priya will share spreadsheets and raw CSVs; Jordan will send pilot pricing and contract; Apex provides 1k prompts + expected QPS by Mar 27. we'll schedule kickoff week of Mar 30.
[18:45] Marta: sounds good.
[18:50] Sunil: small question  do you support forwarder to our SIEM for request-level logs?
[18:58] Liam: yes we'll include a logging plan in the security packet.
[19:10] [small crosstalk, 3 people talking briefly about availability windows]
[19:30] Priya: i uploaded the sim csv and also a slides PDF to the chat: https://redwood.example.com/slides/optimize-quant-walkthrough.pdf
[19:50] Marta: one last thing  do you have references for similar pilots?
[20:00] Jordan: yes we can share anonymized reference notes from two customers in fintech and retail who ran int8 pilots, i'll include in the follow up.
[20:20] Devon: good. thanks everyone.
[20:25] Jordan: thanks all. we'll follow up with docs and pricing.

(Transcript ends  remaining time used for Q&A and off-line security sync; exported files and links posted in chat.)
